summary: node1 now publishes the staged public and authenticated staff trees on TCP 8080 using Apache. All security, preservation, and reboot-persistence checks passed.
actions_performed: Installed RHEL-supported Apache 2.4.63 packages without changing the OS release or kernel.
Configured /public/ for anonymous access and /staff/ for HTTP Basic authentication as reader.
Created a bcrypt password database with mode 0640; the password was never printed.
Disabled directory indexes and denied access to source and generated password files.
Applied persistent firewalld and SELinux rules for TCP 8080 and enabled Apache at boot.
Preserved the supplied four files byte-for-byte and retained a root-only Apache rollback copy.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified automatic recovery with a changed boot identity.

evidence.summary: RHEL 10 and its original kernel were retained; repository Apache was installed, syntax validated, SELinux/firewall configured, and only port 8080 added.
GET /public/ returned 200 and its body matched the staged public page exactly before and after restart.
Anonymous and incorrect credentials returned 401 without content leakage; reader received 200 and exact staff index and roster content.
Password database is mode 0640, password/source credential URLs and traversal attempts returned 403, missing directories returned 404, and no listing marker was served.
All four staged-file SHA-256 hashes, sizes, ownership, permissions, and file count matched the original baseline.

Captured healthy boot ID 4ebdfa06-919e-48a9-8a15-475d9007662c, acknowledged a native reboot, observed new boot ID 36be650a-9fd1-4ef2-904e-17b3da8a6c5c, and proved service, network, firewall, SELinux, data, authentication, and management-path recovery.
